title: Connected graphs with equal independence number and radius
summary: A classical theorem states that the independence number of any connected graph is at least its radius. In 2007, DeLaViña, Pepper, and Waller proved that every connected graph with equal independence number and radius is traceable. We first give a new short proof of this theorem and then prove two results for graphs of higher connectivity. (1) Every 2-connected graph with equal independence number and radius is Hamiltonian. (2) Every 3-connected graph with equal independence number and radius is Hamiltonian-connected and pancyclic. Several lemmas used in the proofs are of independent interest.

title: Exact Realization of Edge and Induced Three-Vertex Subgraph Counts
summary: The study of three-vertex subgraph densities has developed along two complementary lines: exact finite realization in large graphs of a given order, and asymptotic approximate realization by sequences of graphs. We bridge these viewpoints for the edge density and the four induced three-vertex subgraph densities. By analyzing local modifications of finite samples from graphons, we show that, for any nonempty subset of these densities, every asymptotically feasible target vector lying a fixed positive distance from the boundary of the corresponding feasible region is realized exactly by a graph of every sufficiently large order, subject only to the natural arithmetic constraints. Thus, in the interior of these feasible regions, asymptotic feasibility implies exact finite realizability up to the unavoidable arithmetic obstructions.

title: An elementary proof of a tight $Δ+1$ bound for the additive chromatic number
summary: An additive coloring assigns positive integer labels to the vertices of a graph so that adjacent vertices have different sums of their neighbors' labels. The additive chromatic number $η(G)$ is the least $k$ for which labels from $[k]$ suffice. We give an elementary orientation argument proving that every finite simple graph $G$ satisfies $η(G) \leq Δ(G) + 1$. This argument yields a $(Δ(G) + 1)$-additive-coloring in polynomial time and improves upon the current best bound of $η(G) \leq Δ(G)^{2} - Δ(G) + 1$, valid for $Δ(G) \geq 2$, from Akbari, Ghanbari, Manaviyat, and Zare.

title: Inverting Dependently Random Tournaments
summary: Let $\text{inv}(T)$ be the inversion index of the tournament $T$. Answering a question of Behague, we show that $\text{inv}(T_1\to T_2)=\text{inv}(T_1)+\text{inv}(T_2)$ does not even hold asymptotically.

title: Syzygy and Adjoint Matroids
summary: We give a matroid-theoretic analogue of Gaussian elimination and use it to construct, for every matroid M, the syzygy matroid Syz(M) on the collection of circuits of M. Dualizing the construction yields the combinatorial adjoint Adj(M) on the collection of maximal proper flats of M, and the two are related by Adj(M) \simeq Syz(M*). Neither construction depends on a realization. We determine Syz(M) when M is U_{k,k+3} or the Vamos matroid V_{8}. We also show that Adj(M) is an adjoint of M when M has rank 3. When M has rank 4 and V_{8} is a restriction of M, Adj(M) has rank 3 and is not an adjoint of M.

title: Cographs in chordal graphs
summary: For a graph $G$, let $\text{cg}(G)$ be the maximum $k\in \mathbb N$ for which $G$ contains a $k$-vertex cograph as an induced subgraph. The Erdős-Hajnal conjecture asserts that for every proper hereditary graph class $\mathcal{G}$, there exists $γ\in(0,1]$ such that every $n$-vertex graph $G\in\mathcal{G}$ satisfies $\text{cg}(G)\geq n^γ$. This is still open; however, for some hereditary classes, one may guarantee much stronger bounds. For instance, every chordal graph $G$ on $n\geq 2$ vertices satisfies $\text{cg}(G)\geq n/(2\log n)$. Paul Seymour asked whether this bound is optimal up to a constant factor. We answer this affirmatively, even for interval graphs: For every integer $n\geq 2$, we construct an $n$-vertex interval graph $G$ with $\text{cg}(G)<64n/\log n$.

title: Permutation classes need not have proper growth rates
summary: By the Marcus-Tardos Theorem (formerly the Stanley-Wilf Conjecture), every permutation class other than the class of all permutations has a finite upper growth rate, meaning that the $n$th root of the number of permutations of length $n$ in the class has a finite limit superior. It has long been conjectured that this limit superior is in fact always a proper limit. We disprove this by constructing a permutation class whose upper and lower growth rates differ. The construction uses grid classes with cubic row-column graphs of increasing girth, obtained from Haar graphs of finite 2-groups. The corresponding hereditary property of ordered graphs also disproves an analogous 2006 conjecture of Balogh, Bollobás, and Morris. Along the way, we show that every proper permutation class with a D-finite generating function has a proper growth rate. We also establish refined enumerative bounds for grid classes, which lead to a short proof of Albert and Vatter's generalization of Bevan's Theorem on the growth rates of grid classes.

title: Asymptotical results on the automorphism groups of canonical double cover of graphs
summary: The canonical double cover $BX$ of a graph $X$ is the direct product $X\times K_2$. A graph $X$ is stable if every automorphism of $BX$ is induced by automorphisms of $X$ and $K_2$, and unstable otherwise. We prove several asymptotic results on stable and unstable graphs. In particular, we show that the automorphism group of the canonical double cover of almost every graph has order $2$, and consequently that almost all graphs are stable. We also prove that the dominant sources of instability are having twins and being disconnected, in that order, and that graphs arising from a known construction are the next step in this hierarchy.

title: A remoteness formula for generalized Wythoff games
summary: Smith's remoteness function records how long an impartial game lasts when the winner wins as quickly as possible and the loser delays defeat. For the generalized Wythoff game $\mathrm{WYT}(a,b)$, in which two positive integer parameters $a$ and $b$ determine which simultaneous removals from the two piles are allowed, we give a formula for the remoteness of every position, building on the known values at losing positions. The formula depends on two indices: a local index determined by the coordinates of the losing positions in a window of length $b$ ending at the smaller pile, and the integer part of the pile difference divided by $a$. When $b=1$, complementary Beatty sequences make the local index explicit, which gives an explicit formula for $\mathrm{WYT}(a,1)$, including classical Wythoff's game. We also show that if each attempted move in a finite impartial game independently fails with a fixed probability and passes the turn, the probability that the player to move wins under optimal play is an explicit exponential function of remoteness. For every success probability strictly between $0$ and $1$, the optimal attempts are exactly the moves that reduce remoteness by one.

title: Finiteness theorems for Cayley permutation classes
summary: We prove that every hereditary Cayley permutation class with finitely many simple members has a finite basis and an algebraic generating function. We first show that every simple Cayley permutation of length at least two contains a simple pattern obtained by deleting one or two letters, and that the only exceptional Cayley permutations are the simple parallel alternations and their symmetries. We then characterize substitution-closed classes by the simplicity of their basis elements and show that classes with finitely many simple members are partially well ordered. Given the simple members and the basis of such a class, we construct a finite system of functional equations and compute an annihilating polynomial.

title: A note on the proof of Barnette's conjecture
summary: Barnette's conjecture states that every cubic 3-connected bipartite planar graph has a Hamiltonian cycle. We present a digested exposition of OpenAI's generated proof of Barnette's conjecture \cite{openai-barnette}.

title: The linearity Conjecture
summary: The Linearity Conjecture states that in the projective plane PG(2,$q$), $q=p^h$, every minimal blocking set (w.r.t. lines) is a linear point set over some subfield of ${\mathbb F}_q$. This paper contains the proof of the Linearity Conjecture for $p^e\ne 3,4$, where $e$ is the exponent of the blocking set. The text contains 3 concatenated parts. In Part 0, we give a guide for reading Parts 1 and 2. Part 1 develops a great part of the method, and the case $p^e=2$ is solved. In Part 2 we prove the Linearity Conjecture for $p^e\geq 5$.

title: Asymptotically Sharp Length Thresholds for \texorpdfstring{$q$}{q}-ary Codes with Distances \texorpdfstring{$2$}{2} and \texorpdfstring{$4$}{4}
summary: For an integer $q\ge5$, let $A_q(n,\{2,4\})$ be the largest cardinality of a subset of a $q$-ary Hamming space of length $n$ in which every two distinct words have distance $2$ or $4$. Set \[ N(q)=\left\lceil\max\left\{2q+1, \frac{17+\sqrt{8q^2+96q-95}}2\right\}\right\rceil. \] We prove that $A_q(n,\{2,4\})=1+\binom n2$ for every $n\ge N(q)$. In particular, $N(q)=2q+1$ for $q\ge26$. An explicit code of size $q(n-2)$ shows that the least eventual threshold $N_*(q)$ satisfies $N_*(q)\ge2q-1$; consequently $2q-1\le N_*(q)\le2q+1$ for every $q\ge26$. The argument applies to arbitrary integer alphabet sizes, without a linearity assumption. Its main ingredients are synchronization of symbols on intersecting supports, weighted bounds for $2$-intersecting families of four-sets, and a joint estimate for the weight-two and weight-four layers in a common-three-core configuration. No computational verification is required.

title: The Ternary and Quaternary Cases of the $\{2,4\}$-Distance Code Conjecture
summary: For an integer $q\ge2$, let $A_q(n,\{2,4\})$ be the largest cardinality of an unrestricted $q$-ary code of length $n$ in which any two distinct words have Hamming distance $2$ or $4$. We prove that \[ A_q(n,\{2,4\})=1+\binom n2 \qquad(q\in\{3,4\},\ n\ge6), \] thereby settling the two remaining alphabet sizes in the conjecture of Boyvalenkov, Delchev, Zinoviev, and Zinoviev; the binary case was settled previously. The quaternary result implies the ternary result by alphabet inclusion. For $n\ge16$, the quaternary upper bound is proved combinatorially. After normalizing one word to zero, the weight-four supports form a $2$-intersecting family; exact support intersections force symbol synchronization and restrict support multiplicities. We combine the nontrivial intersection theorem with matching arguments and a three-coordinate projection lemma. The finite lengths $6\le n\le13$ are handled by a complete Hamming-isometry reduction to exact clique decisions, and $n=14,15$ by a smaller exact weighted-clique relaxation. All finite decisions are reproduced by two standalone integer-only C++17 verifiers provided as supplementary source files.

title: NP-Hardness of Generalized-Turán Graph Modification Problems
summary: For graphs $G, T$ and a graph-family $\mathcal{H}$, let $ex(G,T,\mathcal{H})$ denote the maximum possible number of copies of $T$ in an $\mathcal{H}$-free subgraph of $G$. Alon and Shikhelman conjectured that for every family of graphs $\mathcal{H}$ with $χ(H) > s$ for every $H \in \mathcal{H}$, it is NP-hard to compute $ex(G,K_s,\mathcal{H})$, and even to approximate it up to additive error $n^{s-δ}$ on $n$-vertex graphs, for any fixed $δ> 0$. The case $s=2$ was established in a breakthrough result of Alon, Shapira and Sudakov. We prove the Alon-Shikhelman conjecture for finite families $\mathcal{H}$. In particular, we obtain an elementary proof of the Alon-Shapira-Sudakov result when $\mathcal{H}$ is finite.

title: Aleshin graphs are expanders
summary: We prove that the Aleshin level graphs are two-sided expanders. We establish linear diameter bounds for Belaterra and Aleshin graph families. At level $n$, the diameters of the Bellaterra and undirected Aleshin graphs are a $|V_n|=2^n$. This improves the quadratic diameter bounds of Malyshev and Pak to the correct order of growth. For the Aleshin graphs we obtain a normalized spectral gap of at least $1-2\sqrt2/3$ and an edge-expansion constant of at least $3-2\sqrt2$, thereby establishing a Malyshev--Pak's Conjecture with explicit constants. An exact calculation at level ten also proves that the undirected Aleshin graphs are not Ramanujan for any $n\geq10$.

title: On Arithmetic-Progression Biases in Random Partitions: Limiting Laws and the Li-Zhao Conjecture
summary: Let $\cR=\{r+jm:j\geq0\}$ and $\cS=\{s+jm:j\geq0\}$ be disjoint arithmetic progressions of positive integers, and choose a partition of $n$ uniformly at random. We determine the limiting probability that the number of parts in $\cR$ is larger than the number of parts in $\cS$. More precisely, if $a=r/m$ and $b=s/m$, then this probability converges to $I_{1/2}(a,b)$, the regularized incomplete beta function. We prove the stronger distributional statement that, after multiplication by the partition saddle-point parameter, the difference of the two numbers of parts converges to $m^{-1}(\log G_b-\log G_a)$, where $G_a$ and $G_b$ are independent gamma variables. The proof uses the Boltzmann conditioning device for random partitions, a $q$-gamma evaluation of the unconditioned characteristic function, and a uniform Fourier estimate showing that conditioning on the total size does not change the limit. We also evaluate the finite-truncation limit studied by Li and Zhao. The two evaluations coincide, proving their conjecture on the commutation of the truncation and large-size limits.

title: Fuglede's conjecture holds in $\mathbb{F}_{p}^{d}$ for $p=2,\,d=8$ and $p=11,\,d=3$
summary: Fuglede's conjecture in $\mathbb{F}_p^d$ says that a nonempty set tiles by translation if and only if it is spectral. We prove the conjecture in $\mathbb{F}_2^8$ and $\mathbb{F}_{11}^3$. Over $\mathbb{F}_2$ we show more generally that the Fourier support of a nonconstant indicator of density different from one half contains a plane. Consequently every spectral set of density one quarter has a subspace tiling complement. This supplies one of the dimension-eight reductions left by Kadowaki; the others are completed using classified Hadamard matrices and perfect binary codes. In $\mathbb{F}_2^9$ we prove that every tile is spectral and that every spectral set has power-of-two cardinality. All spectral cardinalities except $64$ are shown to tile, and we give further reductions of the remaining case. We also construct a spectral set of density one eighth whose Fourier support contains no three-dimensional subspace. For $\mathbb{F}_{11}^3$ we extend the geometric method of Fallon, Mayeli, and Villano by using moment identities, polynomial plane profiles, weighted incidence counts, and exact finite computations. The computations and their verification programs are described in the appendices.

title: Weighted odd-cycle transversals and fractional colorings of planar graphs
summary: We bound fractional chromatic numbers by establishing a connection with low-weight odd-cycle transversals. Let $\ell\geq 3$ be an integer and let $G$ be a graph of odd girth at least $\ell$ whose odd-cycle covering polyhedron is integral. For every nonnegative weight vector $w=(w_v)_{v\in V(G)}\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^{V(G)}$, we obtain a set $Z\subseteq V(G)$ such that $G-Z$ is bipartite and $w(Z)\leq\frac{mad(G)}{2\ell}w(V(G))$. Here, $w(S)=\sum_{v\in S}w_v$ for any $S\subseteq V(G)$, and $mad(G)$ denotes the maximum average degree of $G$. Consequently, if $mad(G)<2\ell$, then $G$ has fractional chromatic number at most $\frac{4\ell}{2\ell-mad(G)}$. As applications, we prove that, for every positive integer $k$, every $n$-vertex planar graph of girth at least $2k+3$ has fractional chromatic number at most $\frac{2k+1}{k}(1-\frac{1}{kn+1})$, establishing the girth version of Naserasr's fractional coloring conjecture with a strict inequality. For $k=1$, we furthermore prove that the upper bound $\frac{3n}{n+1}$ holds for every $n$-vertex triangle-free planar graph and this is attained for infinitely many values of $n$.

title: Probabilistic and game thresholds
summary: Let $X$ be a finite set and $\mathcal{F} \subseteq 2^X$ a non-trivial increasing property. We show that the bias-threshold $b(\mathcal{F})$ for the Picker-Chooser $\mathcal{F}$-game satisfies $b(\mathcal{F}) \ge α/ p_c(\mathcal{F})$, where $p_c(\mathcal{F})$ is the threshold for the property $\mathcal{F}$ and $α> 0$ is an absolute constant. This proves that Picker-Chooser games satisfy one-sided ``probabilistic intuition''. The proof is based on the notion of influence from the theory of boolean functions.

title: Arithmetic Conditions for the Invertibility of Circulant Matrices over Finite Fields
summary: This paper investigates arithmetic conditions, over finite fields, for the invertibility of circulant matrices whose first row is $(a_0,\ldots,a_{n-1})$, in terms of linear constraints on the entries $a_0,\ldots,a_{n-1}$. The coefficients of such linear constraints are determined by field traces arising from Frobenius orbits of roots of unity, and under additional assumptions they are given by Ramanujan sums reduced modulo the characteristic of the given field. These results provide finite-field analogues of the corresponding criteria over $\mathbb{Q}$, where the relevant Ramanujan-sum linear constraints can be formulated without such additional assumptions, while also showing some differences caused by reduction modulo the characteristic. The constraints can often determine invertibility using aggregate information about the entries of a row, rather than the particular pattern of the entries. We also discuss the polynomial gcd criterion, which gives necessary and sufficient conditions for invertibility and yields further consequences for special families of circulant matrices.

title: The signless Laplacian spectral Turán problems for disjoint triangles
summary: The classical Turán-type problem for graphs forbidding $k$ disjoint triangles has been resolved firstly by Erdős [Arch. Math. 13 (1962) 222-227] for graphs of sufficiently large order and improved by Moon [Canad. J. Math. 20 (1968) 95-102], who established that the unique edge extremal graph is $K_{k-1}\vee T_2(n-k+1)$ for $n> \frac{19k-11}{2}$. In this paper, we determine the maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius among all $kK_3$-free graphs of order $n$ and characterize the unique signless Laplacian spectral extremal graph $K_{k-1}\vee T_{2}(n-k+1)$ for all $k\ge 2$ and sufficiently large $n$.

title: On the maximal index of $C_4^-$-free unbalanced signed graphs of prescribed size
summary: The extremal problem of determining the graphs with maximum spectral radius among all graphs with a prescribed number of edges was resolved by Rowlinson [Linear Algebra Appl. 110 (1988) 43--53]. A signed graph $Γ=(G,σ)$ is called $C_k^-$-free if it contains no negative $k$-cycle as a signed subgraph. The index of a signed graph is defined as the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix. This paper addresses the maximization of the index of unbalanced signed graphs. For signed graphs of a prescribed order, Wang and Lin [Discrete Appl. Math. 372 (2025) 164--172] determined the maximum index of $C_4^{-}$-free unbalanced signed graphs. Subsequently, Wang, Peng and Hou [Discrete Math. 349 (2026) 114871] characterized the unbalanced signed graphs of prescribed size with maximum index. This paper treats the edge spectral Turán-type problem for $C_4^-$-free unbalanced signed graphs. The all-positive signed graph with underlying graph $G$ is denoted by $(G,+)$. Evidently, $A((G,+))=A(G)$. In particular, $(H_{d,t},+)$ is the all-positive signed graph whose underlying graph is $H_{d,t}$, where $H_{d,0}=K_d$ and for $t>0$, $H_{d,t}$ is obtained from $K_d$ by adding a single vertex adjacent to exactly $t$ vertices of $K_d$. Let $m-3=\binom{d}{2}+t$ with $0\le t\le d-1$. Up to switching isomorphism and the addition of isolated vertices, the unique extremal unbalanced signed graph is obtained by attaching a negative triangle to a specified vertex of the all-positive signed graph $(H_{d,t},+)$.

title: Spectral and edge conditions for negative Hamiltonian cycles in unbalanced signed graphs
summary: Spectral conditions for Hamiltonian cycles are a fundamental subject in extremal spectral graph theory. For simple unsigned graphs, Fiedler and Nikiforov [Linear Algebra Appl., 432 (2010), 2170-2173] pioneered this direction, and Li and Ning [Linear Multilinear Algebra, 64 (2016), 2252-2269] later extended these results by introducing minimum degree parameters. In this paper, we study the spectral conditions for the existence of a negative Hamiltonian cycle in unbalanced signed graphs of order n > 8. We first determine the maximum index among all n-vertex unbalanced signed graphs containing no negative Hamiltonian cycle, and characterize the corresponding extremal graphs up to switching isomorphism. Furthermore, we establish an upper bound on the number of edges in unbalanced signed graphs of order n >= 7 with frustration index one, and classify all extremal graphs achieving this bound.

title: Two refined Wilf-equivalences for patterns of length 4 and a conjecture on Dumont permutations of the first kind
summary: We construct a bijection between $2143$-avoiding and $3421$-avoiding permutations that preserves the descent top set and the ascent top set and reverses the left-to-right order of the peaks. This bijection allows us to establish a bijection between $1243$-avoiding and $3412$-avoiding permutations with the same properties. These results refine two cases of a conjecture posed by Burstein and prove a conjecture posed by Burstein and Jones.

title: Nonexistence of Constant Congruences for the Cumulative Partition Function
summary: Let $p(n)$ be the ordinary partition function and let $c(n)=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}p(k)$, with $c(0)=0$. We prove that, for every $a\geq1$, $b\geq0$, and $m\geq2$, the sequence $c(an+b)$ is not eventually constant modulo $m$, thereby answering a question posed by Chen. The proof combines the algebraicity over $\mathbb C(j)$ of modular functions for finite-index subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)$ with Voloch's theorem on the transcendence of elliptic modular functions in positive characteristic.

title: Zero Forcing, Support Varieties, and Boundary Complexes
summary: Let a finite simple graph be given. We study symmetric matrices with this graph pattern that admit a null vector with prescribed exact support. Such a vector exists precisely when its support is a fort, meaning that no vertex outside the support has exactly one neighbor inside it. Over the complex numbers, we prove that the Zariski closure of each exact-support coefficient locus is irreducible and compute its codimension in terms of boundary vertices and a labeled forest on the connected components of the support. The corresponding forest deficiency also determines the generic restricted nullity. An incidence parametrization yields a prime decomposition of the reduced zero-forcing failure locus. For a prescribed common kernel, we describe the coefficient space through equilibrium stresses, exterior affine dependencies, and free coefficients. We then construct boundary complexes recording local solution values and equation residuals. Their gluing maps are defined over the universal coefficient ring and commute with arbitrary base change. By retaining the complete collection of support signatures associated with each seed set, we obtain a composition formula for the minimum zero-forcing number and an algorithm for its computation.

title: Zero Forcing on Maximal Outerplanar Graphs: Capacities and Phase Repair
summary: We determine the zero-forcing number of maximal biconnected outerplanar graphs. When the weak dual is a path, the zero-forcing number and the induced path-covering number are both two. Otherwise, the branching faces determine a canonical core and a family of terminal strips. We prove that an optimal forcing process can be chosen in a normal form governed by explicit vertex and face capacities on the core. After fixing forests on the terminal strips, the zero-forcing number is expressed through an optimization over core-edge selections and the minimum number of root connections that must be removed to obtain an executable orientation. The path-covering number is obtained from the same capacity optimization without the repair cost. We characterize executable orientations by blocking-circuit equations and identify the two-path obstruction with a first cohomology class of a signed contact multigraph. Local replacements and a finite comparison of boundary recurrences establish the normal form for graphs of arbitrary size. A fifty-six-state recurrence constructs a minimum zero-forcing set and a complete forcing chronology in linear time from indexed triangle adjacency. We also obtain exact replacement results for rooted blocks and construct infinite families in which the zero-forcing number exceeds the path-covering number.

title: An algebraic proof of 1-extension
summary: We give a new proof that 1-extension preserves generic local rigidity of bar-joint frameworks in all dimensions. The proof does not use a special position argument, which makes the approach potentially useful for X-replacement in 3-space. Instead, the balancing conditions recently introduced by the first author use directed paths in the line graph, and by modifying the end of these paths, we transfer a self-stress on the 1-extended graph back to the original. Treating the new vertex as variable allows us to extract the balancing condition of the smaller graph as one coefficient of a homogeneous quadratic. A Lean 4 formalization of the main results accompanies the paper.

title: A new lower bound for the sixth Schur number: $S(6)\ge 537$
summary: We give an explicit partition of $\{1,\ldots,537\}$ into six sum-free sets, establishing $S(6)\ge 537$. This improves the lower bound 536 of Fredricksen and Sweet (2000). Known recursive constructions then give the improved lower bounds $S(8)\ge 5\,372$, $S(11)\ge 204\,208$, $S(13)\ge 2\,042\,082$, and $R_6(3)\ge 539$. We also report 131 pairwise inequivalent partitions found by the search. We describe their structure and provide the complete partitions in the supplementary material. These partitions provide starting points for future searches and structural studies of Schur partitions.

title: Prime Nullspace Matrices and Even Dominating Sets
summary: A non-zero $m \times n$ (0, 1)-matrix $A$ is called a {\em nullspace matrix} if each entry $(i, j)$ of $A$ has an even number of $1's$ in the set of entries consisting of $(i, j)$ and its rectilinear neighbors. These matrices correspond to even dominating sets of $m \times n$ grid graphs. We study these matrices and consider those that cannot be constructed from smaller nullspace matrices.

title: Water Transport on 3-Spiders: Unbounded Lengths of Shortest Optimal Strategies
summary: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph. An averaging operation selects a nonempty connected vertex set and replaces the weights of its vertices by their arithmetic mean. For a nonnegative initial weight function $ω:V(G)\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$ and a target vertex $x$, let $t(G,x,ω)$ denote the minimum number of averaging operations needed to attain the maximum reachable weight at $x$. Gollin et al.[1] proved, using the Axiom of Choice, that a finite optimal strategy exists for every finite graph, every nonnegative initial weight function and every target vertex; see Tao [2] for a simplified proof. We prove that the lengths of shortest optimal strategies on $3$-spiders have no uniform finite bound. In particular, these lengths cannot be bounded in terms of the maximum degree of the graph.

title: Functions determining $(q+3)/2$ directions over the finite field with $q$ elements
summary: Let $q=p^n$, where $p>2$ is prime. We prove that every $q$-set $U\subseteq\mathrm{AG}(2,q)$ determining exactly $(q+3)/2$ directions is affinely equivalent to the graph of $x^{(q+1)/2}$. For $n\ge2$, we also prove that a $q$-set determining at most $(q+p)/2$ directions is either an affine $\mathbb{F}_p$-linear set or affinely equivalent to this graph. The classification for $n=1$ is due to Lovász and Schrijver. For $n=2$, the classification and the stated stability result follow from results of Gács, Lovász, and Sz\H onyi and the direction theorems of Blokhuis, Ball, Brouwer, Storme, and Sz\H onyi, completed by Ball. These direction theorems establish affine $\mathbb{F}_p$-linearity for functions with fewer than $(q+3)/2$ determined directions. Our proof uses Rédei polynomials, results of Gács, Lovász, and Sz\H onyi on their coefficients, and an earlier polynomial comparison lemma of the author.

title: Triple Quantum Schubert Calculus
summary: We prove a triple quantum Pieri formula: the product of a quantum double Schubert polynomial $\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_u(x;y)$ by a quantum factorial elementary polynomial $\widetilde{E}_{p,k}(x;z)$ in a second set of variables $z$ is a sum over chains in the quantum Bruhat graph, indexed by a quantum analogue of Sottile's relation, whose coefficients are monomials in the quantum parameters times polynomials in the differences $y_i-z_j$ with nonnegative integer coefficients, and which is Graham-positive at $z=y$. At $y=z=0$ it is the quantum Pieri rule of Ciocan-Fontanine and Postnikov; at $z=y$ it is an equivariant quantum Pieri rule for the complete flag variety, indexed by chains in the quantum Bruhat graph rather than, as in the rule of Huang and Li, by the data of a reduction to classical cohomology, and proved directly. A doubled Pieri formula, positive in the same senses, treats multiplication by the quantization of a product of two elementary polynomials in the same variables, which is not the product of the quantizations: it is two iterated Pieri steps with the incompatible pairs of chains omitted. More generally, the triple quantum Schubert structure constants $c_{u,v}^{w,d}(y;z)$, the coefficients of $\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_u(x;y)\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_v(x;z)$ in the basis $\{\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_w(x;y)\}$, are polynomials in the $y_i-z_j$ with nonnegative integer coefficients; the proof of this appears as an appendix. We extend the Peterson-Woodward comparison formula and the quantum-to-classical reduction of Leung-Li and Huang-Li to the triple constants, and we describe and prove correct the algorithms of schubmult, which compute products of arbitrary quantum double Schubert polynomials well beyond the reach of previous methods.
comment: 57 pages. Includes an appendix by Tongren Xiao and Yihua Yue proving triple quantum Schubert positivity. Algorithms implemented in the Python package schubmult

title: The domination number of the 2-token graph of the complete bipartite graph
summary: For a graph $G$, the $2$-token graph $F_2(G)$ has as vertices all $2$-subsets of $V(G)$, with two such subsets adjacent whenever their symmetric difference is an edge of $G$. In this paper, we determine the domination number of the $2$-token graph of the complete bipartite graph $K_{m,n}$, for all integers $2\le m\le n$. We show that it equals $\lceil m/2\rceil+n-1$, except when $m=3$, or when $m\ge5$ is odd and $n=m+1$; in these two exceptional situations it is one less. Our arguments rely on an explicit characterization of the dominating sets of the $2$-token graph of $K_{m,n}$.
comment: 14 pages, 3 Figures, 1 Table. Submitted for publication before the appearance of arXiv:2610.28936, whose results on F_2(K_{m,n}) were obtained independently. This version differs from the submitted one only by a footnote on arXiv:2610.28936 and three added references in the conclusions section

title: Conway's thrackle conjecture: a new upper bound of $\frac43n$
summary: A thrackle is a drawing of a graph in the plane in which every pair of edges meets exactly once, either at a common endpoint or at a proper crossing. Conway conjectured that every thrackle has at most as many edges as vertices. We prove that every thrackle on $n\ge4$ vertices has at most $\left\lfloor4(n-1)/3\right\rfloor$ edges. The proof combines Pammer's computer-assisted verification of the conjecture for graphs on at most twelve vertices with a discharging argument in suitable plane and projective-plane embeddings.

title: Triple parabolic cosets have unique Bruhat minima
summary: A folklore result says that any parabolic double coset $W_{I} w W_{J}$ in a Coxeter group $W$ is an interval of the Bruhat order, provided that $W_{I}$ and $W_{J}$ are finite. We include a self-contained proof, without assuming that $W$ is finite. Furthermore, we prove that each "triple coset" $W_{I} u W_{J} v W_{K}$ has a Bruhat minimum and -- if $W_{I}, W_{J}, W_{K}$ are finite -- a Bruhat maximum, but (in general) is not a Bruhat interval. This proves and extends a conjecture on MathOverflow #472072.
comment: 20 pages, includes expository material, comments are welcome

title: Quantum K-structure constants and cylindric Grothendieck polynomials for Grassmannians
summary: We use the partition functions of a five-vertex exactly solvable lattice model from statistical mechanics to give new combinatorial formulae for the Schubert structure constants of torus-equivariant quantum K-theory rings of Grassmannians. The proofs build on our earlier results where we identified the transfer matrices of these lattice models geometrically as multiplications by the Hirzebruch $λ_y$ classes of the tautological subbundle and the (dual) quotient bundle. The structure constants are solutions of a system of linear equations with coefficients given by the partition function. This system may be solved explicitly by specializing the Hirzebruch parameter $y$ to an equivariant parameter, leading to explicit formulae using Cramer's rule. Furthermore, we give an alternative combinatorial construction of the partition functions in terms of sums over cylindric set-valued tableaux, which we call cylindric Grothendieck polynomials. The latter generalise McNamara's factorial skew Grothendieck and Yeliussizov's modified Grothendieck polynomials and can be thought of as an equivariant K-theoretic version of Postnikov's toric Schur function. We also provide new polynomial representatives for equivariant K-theory classes of Richardson varieties and their variants.

title: The Asymptotic Number of Anticodes in Hamming Spaces
summary: In the Hamming space $\mathbb{F}_q^n$, a $d$-anticode is a subset in which every pair of points has Hamming distance at most $d$, or equivalently, a set of diameter at most $d$. Let $m_q(n,d)$ denote the maximum size of a $d$-anticode and let $\mathcal{A}_q(n,d)$ be the family of all $d$-anticodes. We show that for fixed $q$, as $n\to\infty$, the total number of $d$-anticodes satisfies \[ |\mathcal{A}_q(n,d)|=2^{(1+o(1))m_q(n,d)} \] for $4\le d\le n-1$, except when $q=2$ and $d=n-1$. We also count linear $d$-anticodes, that is, subspaces of $\mathbb F_q^n$ with diameter at most $d$. For fixed $q$ and $d$, their number is polynomial in $n$. For growing $d$, we determine the exponential order as $q^{Θ_q(d^2+d\log_q(n/d))}$ in the sublinear regime and $q^{Θ(n^2)}$ when $d/n\toα\in(0,1)$. In the near-full regime $n-d=o(n)$, we obtain the sharper count $q^{(1/4+o(1))n^2}$. A random-generator construction further improves the binary lower bound for every fixed linear diameter.

title: Simultaneous popular polynomial differences in higher dimensions
summary: We extend the simultaneous popular polynomial difference theorem of Conlon, Dong, and the author to polynomial shifts along prescribed directions in $\mathbb{F}_p^D$. Let $P_1,\ldots,P_k\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ be linearly independent polynomials with zero constant terms, and let $v_1,\ldots,v_k\in\mathbb{Z}^D\setminus\{0\}$. We show that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, every sufficiently large prime $p$, and every $A\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p^D$ of density $α$, there exists a nonzero $d\in\mathbb{F}_p$ such that \[ \mathbb{E}_{\underline{x}\in\mathbb{F}_p^D} \mathbf{1}_A(\underline{x}) \prod_{\substack{1\leq i\leq k\\ ω_i=1}} \mathbf{1}_A\bigl(\underline{x}+P_i(d)v_i\bigr) \geq α^{\,1+\sum_{i=1}^kω_i}-\varepsilon \] simultaneously for every $ω\in\{0,1\}^k$. The main new ingredient is a directional arithmetic regularity decomposition adapted to mixed directional box norms.

title: An explicit elementary proof of no Landau--Siegel zeros
summary: We give an elementary proof of the absence of Landau--Siegel zeros with the explicit constant $c=1/100$. For every primitive quadratic Dirichlet character $χ$ of conductor $q\ge3$, each real zero $β\in(0,1)$ of $L(s,χ)$ satisfies $(1-β)\log q>c$. The proof combines integer coefficient counting, polynomial congruences, a paired-tail hyperbola estimate, and a logarithmically weighted comparison of positive sums. All required constants are explicit, and one choice of parameters covers every conductor. The argument uses elementary arithmetic and real summation and integration, without separate zero computations for small conductors.

title: Norm-Euclideanity in cyclic fields
summary: Consider a cyclic number field of prime degree $p$. For a fixed degree, there are only finitely many such fields which are norm-Euclidean. When $p=2$ or $3$, these have been completely determined. If instead $p>3$, one can bound the discriminant of such fields from above. We substantially sharpen these upper bounds via an explicit Burgess-type criterion and describe a method for completely resolving other small prime cases.

title: On the Open Problem in the 2023 Simon Marais Mathematics Competition
summary: We prove that, for $n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$ not a perfect square, the only pairs of positive integers $\{a, b\}$ for which there exists $r \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $r^a + \sqrt{n}$ and $r^b + \sqrt{n}$ are both rational numbers are those of the form $\{a, a\}$ or $\{g, 2g\}$ (with $g$ odd). This resolves an open question presented in the 2023 Simon Marais Mathematics Competition.

title: Aspects of quadratic Chabauty via modular forms
summary: We develop algorithms to construct a basis of de Rham cohomology for modular curves and a matrix representing the Hodge filtration required in the quadratic Chabauty method. We do this without requiring an explicit plane model of the curve and instead compute these objects in terms of modular forms. Our approach works for any modular curve; to demonstrate its efficiency, we implement our method for nonsplit Cartan modular curves.

title: Complete Determination of the Gallai--van der Waerden Number \(\mathrm{GW}(r;3,3)\)
summary: This paper completely determines the Gallai--van der Waerden number \(\mathrm{GW}(r;3,3)\) for all integers \(r\ge 3\): \[ \mathrm{GW}(3;3,3)=\mathrm{GW}(4;3,3)=9,\qquad \mathrm{GW}(r;3,3)=r\quad (r\ge 5). \]

title: OpenAI partially disproves Littlewood's 1961 $L^α$-flat theorem
summary: We present a counterexample, produced by OpenAI, to Littlewood's 1961 theorem on $L^α$-flat polynomials. The theorem asserts that no $L^α$-flat polynomials exist within the class of trigonometric polynomials of the form$$\sum_{m=1}^{n} a_m \cos(mθ+α_m), \qquad n \in \mathbb{N}^*,$$satisfying$$k\, n^2 \sum_{m=1}^{n} a_m^2 \;\leq\; \sum_{m=1}^{n} m^2 a_m^2,$$where $k$ is an absolute constant (alternatively expressed on the right-hand side as $K = 1/k$). We show that OpenAI's counterexample is contained within the class of hyper-lacunary sequences. Consequently, it offers only a limited refutation, as such sequences fail to satisfy an implicit assumption of Littlewood's theorem. We also discuss broader questions surrounding this counterexample and provide a brief historical overview.
comment: 9 pages. 4 quotations. 14 references. Comments, feedback and collaboration are welcome

title: The exponent $1/4$ in three complexity bounds: integer bases, continued fractions, and the $(3/2)^n$ steering word
summary: Let $ξ$ be a real algebraic irrational number and $p(n,ξ,b)$ the number of distinct blocks of length $n$ in its base-$b$ expansion. Bugeaud and Evertse proved in 2008 that $p(n,ξ,b)/(n(\log n)^η)$ is unbounded for every $η<1/11$. We prove this for every $η<1/4$. We also prove the analogous bound for the continued fraction expansion of an algebraic number of degree at least three, with every exponent $δ<1/4$. Bugeaud announced this statement in 2013 with an unspecified $δ>0$. Finally, the subword complexity of the steering word of $(3/2)^n$ exceeds $C\,k(\log k)^η$ infinitely often for every $η<1/4$ and every $C$. The three proofs share one count: $\varepsilon^{-1}$ classes times $\varepsilon^{-3}$ subspaces from the quantitative Subspace Theorem of Evertse and Ferretti. The subspaces are then disposed of at the cost of a logarithm, with no further power of $\varepsilon^{-1}$. All three results, and the quantitative Subspace Theorem they rest on, are machine-verified in Lean~4.

title: Irrationality Exponents of Real CM Elliptic Periods and Powers of the Lemniscate Period
summary: We give a determinant proof that every nonzero real period of a nonsingular elliptic curve over $\mathbb Q$ with complex multiplication, measured with a specified nonzero rational invariant differential, has irrationality exponent two. The proof uses an integral origin chart, matched local lengths, an actual compactification and weighted packet map, and arithmetic and analytic estimates for the same selected minor on a rectangular sublattice of the full CM period lattice. For the integral-defined lemniscate period $Ω=2\int_0^1(1-t^4)^{-1/2}\,dt$, we also give the uniform bound $μ(Ω^n)=O(n\log(2n))$ for integers $n\geq1$. Its new arithmetic ingredient clears integration denominators prime by prime while retaining the coefficient order; a one-root norm argument and an analytic estimate at algebraic centers complete the power proof. The two arguments are presented with their different charts and exact dependencies. Lean verifies the new CM determinant argument and rational normalization relative to explicit classical uniformization, CM-lifting and theta inputs; the lemniscate-power endpoint is also verified. The formalization record states the exact classical boundary and theorem references.

title: On the arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula for orthogonal Shimura varieties over a general totally real field
summary: Let $\mathrm{F}/\mathbb{Q}_p$ be a finite extension with $p\ne 2$, and let $V$ be a quadratic space over $\mathrm{F}$ of dimension at least two admitting a self-dual lattice. We prove the local arithmetic Siegel-Weil formula for GSpin Rapoport-Zink spaces formulated by Li and Zhang. We use the global-to-local strategy of Mihatsch and Zhang and its application by Luo. Using a generalization of the prismatic realization functor of Imai, Kato, and Youcis, we construct and study derived special cycles on integral models of SO Shimura varieties and their Rapoport-Zink uniformizations. We derive the local intersection formula from the modularity of special cycles on the generic fiber. As a first application, we prove the corresponding semi-global arithmetic Siegel-Weil identity for orthogonal Shimura varieties over a totally real field $F\ne\mathbb{Q}$.

title: Landau-Siegel zeros over a base field and effective Brauer-Siegel
summary: Let k be a number field. We prove that for every quadratic extension F/k, every real zero beta of L(s, chi_{F/k}) satisfies (1 - beta) log d_F >= c(k) with an effective constant c(k) > 0, and we deduce (through a reduction of Stark) that the Brauer-Siegel theorem holds effectively and uniformly over all Galois extensions K of k, in the form h_K R_K >= c(k) d_K^{1/2} / ((2 pi)^{[K:Q]} log d_K). Stark's effective cases of the Brauer-Siegel theorem were the fields without quadratic subfields, since the quadratic subfields carried the ineffectivity of Siegel's theorem; over a base field k, the first result removes it. Both rely on a uniform bound for Chebotarev sums. Let K/k be a Galois extension with group G, and suppose S is a subset of G containing the identity. For any prime p of k, let delta_p be the proportion of the primes of K above p whose Frobenius lies in S. Then the sum over Np <= X of delta_p log Np / Np is at most (|S|/|G| + epsilon) log X + O(1), uniformly in K, as soon as X >= d_K^C with C depending only on epsilon and the degree [K:Q]. The proof is Kerr's form of the OpenAI argument, simple vanishing at the points (iota theta)_{iota in S}, with theta in a box in O_K, and Masser's zero estimate. The field enters only through Masser's invariant of the lattice of points, which we compute to be [K:Q]/|S| by averaging over the Galois group of the normal closure. Over Q, the determinant method of Green, Barreto, and Kominers gives sharper Chebotarev bounds, and we explain the comparison.

title: Nonvanishing of 2-primary Kolyvagin classes via simultaneous quadratic twists
summary: Let $E/\mathbf{Q}$ be an elliptic curve, let $K=\mathbf{Q}(\sqrt{D})$ satisfy the Heegner hypothesis with $D<-4$, and fix a modular parametrization $\varphi$ with $\varphi(\infty)=O$. Under surjectivity modulo $2^L$, with $L\ge 2$, and a cohomological exclusion condition at level $4$, we construct a finite set of primes $T$ such that, writing $d_T=\prod_{q\in T}(-q)$ and $n_T=\prod_{q\in T}q$, the $2$-Selmer dimensions of $E^{d_T}$ and $E^{d_TD}$ are $0$ and $1$. The support size is bounded in terms of the initial Selmer dimensions, independently of $L$. Inspired by the work of Tian and Tian--Yuan--Zhang on congruent numbers, we construct a point $Q_T$ on the terminal twist and identify its Kummer class with the standard mod-$2$ Kolyvagin class. Using the low-corank $2$-converse and the $2$-primary Birch--Swinnerton-Dyer formula, we prove that its index $m_T$ in the full Mordell--Weil lattice satisfies $v_2(m_T)=v_2(c_\varphi)+\mathfrak{i}(E,K)$. The optimal Manin constant theorem supplies a $2$-indivisible parametrization $\varphi_0$, for which $κ^{\mathrm{std}}_{n_T,1}(\varphi_0)\ne 0$ if and only if $\mathfrak{i}(E,K)=0$. When the intrinsic index vanishes, the minimum terminal support size is $R=\min\{d_2(E),d_2(E^D)\}$, and the normalized standard classes have order $2^M$ for $1\le M\le L$. Full $2$-adic Galois image then gives strong nonvanishing.

title: The longest increasing subsequences of Luce permutations and permutons
summary: We investigate the longest increasing subsequences (LIS) of random permutations distributed under the Luce model with weights $θ_1^{(n)} \ge \ldots \ge θ_n^{(n)}$. Our first main result provides a general formula for the growth rate of the LIS. For example, we get that the LIS of Luce permutations with Sukhatme weights $θ_k^{(n)} = n-k+1$ grows like $\sqrt{n}$. We also give simple conditions for the LIS to be of order $n^β$, for any given $β\in[1/2,1)$. Our second main result states that, if the weights are of the form $θ_k^{(n)} = f\big( (k-1)/n \big)$ for a sufficiently regular function $f$, then the LIS divided by $2\sqrt{n}$ converges in probability to a constant $K(f)$ described by a variational problem. Throughout, we make extensive use of coupling techniques; in particular, to prove our second main result, we argue that Luce random permutations behave similarly to random permutations sampled from the ``Luce permuton''.

title: Upper tail large deviations of regular subgraph counts in sparse random regular graphs
summary: For a $Δ$-regular connected graph $H$ we obtain the upper tail large deviations speed and rate function for the number of copies of $H$ in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, a random $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices, in the regime $np^{Δ/2} \gg (\log n)^{1/(v_H-2)}$ and $p \ll 1$, where $p:=d/n$ and $v_H$ is the number of vertices, and also identify the typical structure of $\mathbb{G}_n^d$ conditioned on this upper tail event. For $Δ\geq 3$, the speed and the rate function are same with those in the Erdős-Rényi setting. In contrast, for $Δ=2$ (i.e.~in case of cycles), due to the degree constraint in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, although speed remains the same the rate function turns out to be different. Moreover, conditioned on the upper tail event of cycle counts in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, we show that the random graph contains a disjoint collection of clique and biclique like structures with probability approaching to one, a stark contrast compared to the Erdős-Rényi setting. In the complementary regime, i.e.~for $1 \ll n^{v_H}p^{e_H} \ll (\log n)^{α^*_H/(α^*_H-1)}$, where $e_H$ is the number of edges in $H$, $α^*_H$ is the fractional independence number of $H$, and $H$ is a strictly balanced graph (and thus including the regular case), we show that the upper tail large deviations speed and rate function for the number of copies of $H$ match with those in the Erdős-Rényi setting. In this regime, we further show that almost all of the unlabeled copies of $H$ conditioned on the upper tail event are edge disjoint.

title: Automorphisms of Twisted Chevalley Groups over Commutative Rings
summary: We classify all abstract automorphisms of the elementary and full twisted Chevalley groups of types ${}^2A_\ell$ ($\ell\geq3$), ${}^2D_\ell$ ($\ell\geq4$), ${}^2E_6$, and ${}^3D_4$ over arbitrary commutative rings, for every invariant isogeny type. The coefficient automorphism $θ$ has order dividing that of the diagram automorphism. We assume that $2$ is invertible and, for triality, that $3$ is invertible as well. Three features distinguish the answer from the usual inner--diagonal and coefficient decomposition. The elementary groups of types ${}^2A_3$ and ${}^2A_4$ admit an additive family of exceptional automorphisms supported at $θ$-fixed maximal ideals with residue field $\mathbb F_3$. In type ${}^2D_4$, diagram automorphisms may vary on idempotent components, subject to compatibility with the involution and the isogeny lattice. In triality, the coefficient automorphisms preserve the trace operator $r\mapsto r+θ(r)+θ^2(r)$ but need not commute with $θ$. We determine which elementary automorphisms extend to the full groups and describe the remaining central factors. A nonzero exceptional unitary factor extends precisely in the simply connected type ${}^2A_3$, giving a classification for the hyperbolic group $\operatorname{SU}_4(R,θ;Q_4)$. The proof glues uniquely determined normalization data for a finite root frame and then recovers the coefficient action from root-subgroup relations.

title: On a finite group in which every non-nilpotent maximal invariant subgroup of order divisible by $p$ is normal
summary: Let $A$ and $G$ be finite groups such that $A$ acts coprimely on $G$ by automorphisms. For any fixed prime divisor $p$ of $|G|$, we prove that if every non-nilpotent maximal $A$-invariant subgroup of $G$ of order divisible by $p$ is normal then $G$ has a Sylow tower and $G$ is $q$-nilpotent or $q$-closed for each prime divisor $q$ of $|G|$.

title: On the generation of the symmetric group by index relations of three prefix reversals
summary: The cubic pancake graphs are Cayley graphs over the symmetric group Sn generated by three prefix reversals. There is the folllowing open problem: characterize all the sets of three prefix reversals that generate Sn. Blanco and Golubyatnikov give a complete solution of the problem when any of the two smallest or the two largest lengths but n are included in a triple of prefix reversals. According to their conjectures, we give some conditions implying a triple of prefix reversals does not generate Sn. Moreover, Using the symmetric groups that can already be generated by three prefix reversals, we can derive some recurrence conditions.

title: Orbits of $p$-Nilpotent Group Actions for Small Primes
summary: Let $G$ be a finite solvable group and $V$ be a faithful completely reducible $G$-module. We improve previous bounds for the sizes of defect groups of blocks of solvable groups through an improved bound on vector stabilizers of $p$-nilpotent groups. Specifically, if $G$ is 2-nilpotent and $2 \nmid |V|$, then there exists $v \in V$ such that $\mathbf{C}_G(v) \leq \mathbf{F}_4(G)$. Similarly, if $G$ is 3-nilpotent and $3 \nmid |V|$, then there exists $v \in V$ such that $\mathbf{C}_G(v) \leq \mathbf{F}_5(G)$. Using these results, we conclude that $d(B) \leq \lfloor \frac{9n}{10} \rfloor$ when $O_p(G) = 1$ for $p = 2$ and $d(B) \leq \lfloor \frac{19n}{21} \rfloor$ when $O_p(G) = 1$ for $p = 3$.

title: Short curves in homogeneous spaces of the unitary group for unitarily invariant norms
summary: Let A be a unital *-subalgebra of $M_n(C)$ and let $M = U(n)/U(A)$, with the quotient Finsler metric induced by a unitarily invariant norm on $u(n)$, normalized so that $||iP|| = 1$ for rank-one projections $P$. This family contains the unitary orbits of Hermitian matrices, in particular flag manifolds and Grassmann manifolds. We prove that if $z_0$ is a minimal lifting of a tangent vector $X$ with $||X||_{\infty} < π/2$, then the one-parameter group $t \mapsto e^{t z_0}\cdot o$ has minimal length among all piecewise smooth curves in $M$ joining its endpoints. The same holds in manifolds $N=SU(n)/(SU(n) \cap A)$ for every Ad-invariant Finsler norm on $su(n)$, not necessarily symmetric (i.e. the unit sphere does not need to be balanced). The proof relies on the convexity of the distance from the identity along geodesic segments, valid for all these norms. We also prove that the ball of radius $π/2$ around the identity, for the spectral norm, is convex along one-parameter segments. This extends known results for the p-Schatten norms with p even, and gives a new proof for the operator norm, where the result is due to Duran, Mata-Lorenzo and Recht.
